subject: Capacity stack-up: Reserved throughput gap impacting FinLytics production
messages:
From: Caroline Wu <caroline.wu@finlytics.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: FinLytics SRE <sre@finlytics.com>
Date: 2026-08-12T09:17:00-07:00
Subject: Production latency + 503 spikes — need immediate help

Hi Karthik,

We started seeing a sharp increase in latency and intermittent 503s across our inference calls this morning (around 08:30 PT). This is affecting our fraud-detection pipelines — customers are observing degraded scoring and alerts are delayed. Attached is a CSV with a slice of request logs + the graph showing the spike.

We are on your reserved Dedicated pool (pool-id: DL-9873-poolA) and were told this was sized for our steady-state load. Can you confirm whether there is any capacity contention, throttling, or ongoing maintenance on your side? We need to know ETA for stabilization and whether we should failover to the hosted API while this is being investigated.

This is impacting our SLAs — please escalate.

Thanks,
Caroline
VP Engineering, FinLytics

Attachment: customer_kpi_log_20260812-0815.csv
Attachment: error_sla_graph.png
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Caroline Wu <caroline.wu@finlytics.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-12T09:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency + 503 spikes — need immediate help

Caroline — thanks for the data. I’m escalating to Eng and Ops now. Quick notes:
- I’ve looped in Vivek (Operations lead) and Neha (SRE) to triage the Dedicated pool.
- We’ll confirm whether autoscaling or throttles hit a cap and report back within 30 minutes.
- If we need to failover, I’ll propose a minimal plan (temporary hostname change + rate-limited burst on hosted).

I’ll run an internal status thread and keep you posted. Apologies for the disruption — we’ll prioritize this.

—Karthik
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-12T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: INTERNAL: Immediate triage — DL-9873 pool pressure and reserved throughput shortfall

Team,

Summary (initial): Dedicated pool DL-9873-poolA is exhibiting sustained queuing and increased p99 latency coincident with a surge in small-chat workloads from FinLytics between 08:20–09:10 PT. Key observations:
- GPU utilization across the pool reached 98% on A100 nodes; scheduler queued ~22% of incoming requests.
- We observed KV-cache miss storm for a popular prompt path (customer model: fl-bert-7b-v2-quant).
- Autoscale failed to add nodes because the reserved capacity limit is hit (customer committed capacity reached).

Immediate mitigations I executed (09:40 PT):
- Enabled burst capacity for FinLytics using short-term credit from reserve buffer (activates extra nodes w/ reduced SLA).
- Enabled model fallback rule: requests that exceed 200ms queue time will be served by smaller quantized variant (fl-bert-3b-quant) — temporary until we restore capacity.
- Added a prefix cache bypass to reduce KV-cache amplification.

What I need from Product/Eng (action items):
1) Confirm whether the quantized fallback is compatible for FinLytics scoring (Neha to validate signal quality).
2) Provide ETA to spin up additional dedicated nodes beyond the reserve buffer (Marissa to coordinate with infra and confirm procurement path if needed).
3) Prepare a customer-facing note with clear timelines and credit options (Karthik/Marissa).

I’m marking this P0 and requesting executive attention if the reserve buffer is insufficient for sustained load. Attaching initial telemetry snapshot.

—Vivek
Head of Operations, Redwood Inference

Attachment: telem_snapshot_20260812-0940.json (stub)
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-12T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: Immediate triage — DL-9873 pool pressure and reserved throughput shortfall

Quick update after signal check:
- Quality on fl-bert-3b-quant fallback appears within acceptable drift for >85% of FinLytics traffic in our sample. A subset of edge prompts (long-context scoring) may degrade; flagging those for follow-up.
- The 503s were concentrated on worker timeouts resulting from queue depth; timeouts prevented graceful fallback in many cases.
- We have a short-term config change to increase worker timeout to 5s for FinLytics routes only (deploying now).

Risks: if load stays at current peak, reserve buffer will exhaust in ~2.5 hours. We need a procurement/commit decision to scale the pool or coordinate a planned throttling window with the customer.

Next steps: Marissa — can you confirm procurement lead time and whether we have capacity in other AZs to pull from? Karthik — please prepare the options for FinLytics (failover to hosted + credit / temporary throttle + partial credit / accelerate capacity commit).

—Neha
SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Caroline Wu <caroline.wu@finlytics.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: FinLytics SRE <sre@finlytics.com>
Date: 2026-08-12T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency + 503 spikes — need immediate help

Karthik / Vivek — thanks for the rapid response and the fallback. The burst helped briefly but we still see elevated error rates; our ops team is seeing cascading alerts. We have strict compliance windows and need predictable throughput — this behavior is not acceptable without a formal remediation and credit plan.

Please confirm:
1) Exact ETA to stabilize (best estimate) and whether the reserve buffer will last through the day.
2) Whether Redwood will apply service credits given the missed SLA.
3) If you are unable to guarantee capacity, we need a concrete failover plan to your hosted endpoint and a clear runbook for DNS + rate-limits.

We expect an exec-level update within the next 3 hours.

Caroline

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-12T11:40:00-07:00
Subject: INTERNAL: Exec ask and procurement acceleration for DL-9873

Folks — quick consolidation for leadership:
- Situation: FinLytics reserved pool hit committed throughput cap; reserve buffer partially used. Customer sees p99 latency > 1.2s and 503s.
- Business impact: Strategic account (annual ARR $2.4M) — risk of churn + escalation to their CTO if unresolved.
- Options for exec decision (short list):
  1) Convert short-term reserve buffer into sustained added nodes (requires approval to draw from capacity commit fund; procurement ETA 24–48h for sustained instances).
  2) Initiate customer failover to hosted (requires signed MOU + rate-limited traffic shift; lower SLA during transition).
  3) Aggressive throttling policy window for non-critical flows during hours of highest load — coordinated with FinLytics.

Requested asks:
- Vivek: precise estimate for reserve buffer exhaustion (confirm in next 10m).
- Executive patch: Please escalate to CFO/Head of Sales for approval on the capacity commit fund if buffer exhausted.
- Karthik: get Caroline’s go/no-go on failover and credit expectation; prepare a short exec note for their CTO.

I’ll draft the customer-facing mutual action plan (attached: mutual_action_plan_draft.docx) and a one-slide exec summary.

—Marissa
VP, Customer Success
